en: Abu al-Tahir Ahmad ibn 'Amr ibn Sarh narrated to me: Ibn Wahb informed us: 'Amr ibn al-Harith informed me, from Abu al-Zubayr al-Makki, that 'Amir ibn Wathilah narrated to him that he heard 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud say: "The wretched is he who was wretched in his mother's womb, and the blessed is he who takes admonition from others." So he went to a man from the Companions of the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) called Hudhayfah ibn Asid al-Ghifari and narrated that to him from the saying of Ibn Mas'ud, and he said: "And how can a man be wretched without having done any deed?" The man said to him: "Do you wonder at that? For indeed I heard the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) say: 'When forty-two nights have passed over the drop of fluid (nutfah), Allah sends an angel to it, who forms it and creates its hearing, its sight, its skin, its flesh, and its bones. Then he says: 'O Lord, male or female?' And your Lord decrees whatever He wills, and the angel writes it down. Then he says: 'O Lord, his lifespan?' And your Lord decrees whatever He wills, and the angel writes it down. Then he says: 'O Lord, his provision?' And your Lord decrees whatever He wills, and the angel writes it down. Then the angel comes out with the scroll in his hand, neither adding to what he was commanded nor subtracting from it.'"

Muhammad ibn 'Abdillah ibn Numayr and Zuhayr ibn Harb narrated to us—and the wording is Ibn Numayr's—they said: Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah narrated to us, from 'Amr ibn Dinar, from Abu al-Tufayl, from Hudhayfah ibn Asid, tracing it back to the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), who said: "The angel enters upon the drop of fluid (nutfah) after it has settled in the womb for forty or forty-five nights, and says: 'O Lord, wretched or blessed?' and both are written down. Then he says: 'O Lord, male or female?' and both are written down; and his deeds, his traces, his lifespan, and his provision are written down. Then the pages are rolled up, and nothing is added to them nor taken away."

'Uthman ibn Abi Shaybah and Ishaq ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, both from Jarir ibn 'Abd al-Hamid; (H) and Ishaq ibn Ibrahim narrated to us: 'Isa ibn Yunus informed us; (H) and Abu Sa'id al-Ashajj narrated to me: Waki' narrated to us; (H) and 'Ubaydullah ibn Mu'adh narrated it to us: my father narrated to us: Shu'bah ibn al-Hajjaj narrated to us—all of them from al-A'mash, with this chain of transmission. He said in the hadith of Waki': "Indeed, the creation of one of you is gathered in his mother's womb for forty nights." And he said in the hadith of Mu'adh from Shu'bah: "forty nights, forty days." As for the hadith of Jarir and 'Isa, it says: "forty days."

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us: Abu Mu'awiyah and Waki' narrated to us; (H) and Muhammad ibn 'Abdillah ibn Numayr al-Hamdani narrated to us—and the wording is his: my father, Abu Mu'awiyah, and Waki' narrated to us, they said: al-A'mash narrated to us, from Zayd ibn Wahb, from 'Abdullah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), and he is the truthful, the believed, narrated to us: "Indeed, the creation of one of you is gathered in his mother's womb for forty days, then he becomes in that a clinging clot ('alaqah) for a like period, then he becomes in that a lump of flesh (mudghah) for a like period. Then the angel is sent to him and breathes the spirit into him, and is commanded with four words: to write down his provision, his lifespan, his deeds, and whether he is wretched or blessed. By Him besides Whom there is no god, one of you may perform the deeds of the people of Paradise until there is nothing between him and it except an arm's length, then the decree overtakes him and he performs the deeds of the people of the Fire and enters it. And one of you may perform the deeds of the people of the Fire until there is nothing between him and it except an arm's length, then the decree overtakes him and he performs the deeds of the people of Paradise and enters it."

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah and Ishaq ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, from Waki'; (H) and Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us; (H) and Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us: 'Abd al-Samad narrated to me; (H) and Ishaq narrated to us: al-Nadr informed us—all of them from Shu'bah, from Abu 'Imran al-Jawni, with the chain of transmission of Hammad ibn Zayd, the like of his hadith, except that in their narration from Shu'bah, other than 'Abd al-Samad: "and the people love him for it." And in the hadith of 'Abd al-Samad: "and the people praise him," just as Hammad said.

Yahya ibn Yahya al-Tamimi, Abu al-Rabi', and Abu Kamil Fudayl ibn Husayn narrated to us—and the wording is Yahya's; Yahya said: "informed us," and the other two said: Hammad ibn Zayd narrated to us, from Abu 'Imran al-Jawni, from 'Abdullah ibn al-Samit, from Abu Dharr, who said: It was said to the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace): "What do you think of a man who does a good deed and people praise him for it?" He said: "That is the early glad tidings of the believer."

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah and Abu Kurayb narrated to us, they said: Abu Mu'awiyah narrated to us; (H) and Ibn Numayr narrated to us: Abu Mu'awiyah and Muhammad ibn 'Ubayd narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Shaqiq, from Abu Musa, who said: A man came to the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace)... and he mentioned the like of the hadith of Jarir from al-A'mash.

Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna and Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, they said: Ibn Abi 'Adi narrated to us; (H) and Bishr ibn Khalid narrated it to me: Muhammad—meaning Ibn Ja'far—informed us, both from Shu'bah; (H) and Ibn Numayr narrated to us: Abu al-Jawwab narrated to us: Sulayman ibn Qarm narrated to us, all of them from Sulayman, from Abu Wa'il, from 'Abdullah, from the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), the like of it.

'Uthman ibn Abi Shaybah and Ishaq ibn Ibrahim narrated to us—Ishaq said: "informed us," and 'Uthman said: Jarir narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Abu Wa'il, from 'Abdullah, who said: A man came to the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) and said: "O Messenger of Allah, what do you say about a man who loves a people but has not joined them?" The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "A person will be with the one he loves."

Qutaybah narrated to us: Abu 'Awanah narrated to us, from Qatadah, from Anas; (H) and Ibn al-Muthanna and Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, they said: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us: Shu'bah narrated to us, from Qatadah: I heard Anas; (H) and Abu Ghassan al-Misma'i and Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, they said: Mu'adh—meaning Ibn Hisham—narrated to us: my father narrated to me, from Qatadah, from Anas, from the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), with this hadith.

Muhammad ibn Yahya ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz al-Yashkuri narrated to me: 'Abdullah ibn 'Uthman ibn Jabalah narrated to us: my father informed me, from Shu'bah, from 'Amr ibn Murrah, from Salim ibn Abi al-Ja'd, from Anas, from the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), the like of it.

'Uthman ibn Abi Shaybah and Ishaq ibn Ibrahim narrated to us—Ishaq said: "informed us," and 'Uthman said: Jarir narrated to us, from Mansur, from Salim ibn Abi al-Ja'd: Anas ibn Malik narrated to us, saying: While the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) and I were leaving the mosque, we met a man at the vestibule of the mosque, and he said: "O Messenger of Allah, when is the Hour?" The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "What have you prepared for it?" He said: The man seemed to be subdued/hesitant, then he said: "O Messenger of Allah, I have not prepared for it much prayer, fasting, or charity, but I love Allah and His Messenger." He said: "Then you will be with the one you love."

Muhammad ibn 'Ubayd al-Ghubari narrated it to us: Ja'far ibn Sulayman narrated to us: Thabit al-Bunani narrated to us, from Anas ibn Malik, from the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), and he did not mention the statement of Anas: "So I love..." and what followed it.

Abu al-Rabi' al-'Ataki narrated to me: Hammad—meaning Ibn Zayd—narrated to us: Thabit al-Bunani narrated to us, from Anas ibn Malik, who said: A man came to the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) and said: "O Messenger of Allah, when is the Hour?" He said: "And what have you prepared for the Hour?" He said: "Love of Allah and His Messenger." He said: "Then you will be with the one you love." Anas said: We never rejoiced over anything after Islam as intensely as we rejoiced over the saying of the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace): "Then you will be with the one you love." Anas said: "And so I love Allah, His Messenger, Abu Bakr, and 'Umar, and I hope to be with them, even though I have not done deeds like theirs."

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah, 'Amr al-Naqid, Zuhayr ibn Harb, Muhammad ibn 'Abdillah ibn Numayr, and Ibn Abi 'Umar narrated to us—and the wording is Zuhayr's—they said: Sufyan narrated to us, from al-Zuhri, from Anas, who said: A man said: "O Messenger of Allah, when is the Hour?" He said: "And what have you prepared for it?" And he did not mention much. He said: "However, I love Allah and His Messenger." He said: "Then you will be with the one you love." Muhammad ibn Rafi' and 'Abd ibn Humayd narrated it to me—'Abd said: "informed us," and Ibn Rafi' said: 'Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us: Ma'mar informed us, from al-Zuhri: Anas ibn Malik narrated to me that a bedouin man came to the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), with the like of it, except that he said: "I have not prepared much for it that I praise myself for."

'Abdullah ibn Maslamah ibn Qa'nab narrated to us: Malik narrated to us, from Ishaq ibn 'Abdillah ibn Abi Talhah, from Anas ibn Malik, that a bedouin said to the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace): "When is the Hour?" The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said to him: "What have you prepared for it?" He said: "Love of Allah and His Messenger." He said: "You will be with the one you love."

Zuhayr ibn Harb narrated to me: Kathir ibn Hisham narrated to us: Ja'far ibn Burqan narrated to us: Yazid ibn al-Asamm narrated to us, from Abu Hurayrah, with a hadith which he traced back to the Prophet: "People are like ores, like ores of silver and gold; the best of them in the pre-Islamic period of ignorance are the best of them in Islam, if they attain understanding. And souls are recruited troops: those that recognize one another come together in affinity, and those that do not know one another diverge."

Qutaybah ibn Sa'id narrated to us: 'Abd al-'Aziz—meaning Ibn Muhammad—narrated to us, from Suhayl, from his father, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "Souls are recruited troops: those that recognize one another come together in affinity, and those that do not know one another diverge."

'Amr al-Naqid narrated to me: Yazid ibn Harun narrated to us: 'Abd al-'Aziz ibn 'Abdillah ibn Abi Salamah al-Majishun informed us, from Suhayl ibn Abi Salih, who said: We were at 'Arafah when 'Umar ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz passed by while he was in charge of the Hajj season, and the people stood up looking at him. So I said to my father: "O father, indeed I see that Allah loves 'Umar ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz." He said: "And why is that?" I said: "Because of the love he has in the hearts of the people." He said: "By your father! I heard Abu Hurayrah narrating from the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace)..." then he mentioned the like of the hadith of Jarir from Suhayl.

Qutaybah ibn Sa'id narrated to us: Ya'qub—meaning Ibn 'Abd al-Rahman al-Qari—narrated to us; and Qutaybah said: 'Abd al-'Aziz—meaning al-Darawardi—narrated to us; (H) and Sa'id ibn 'Amr al-Ash'athi narrated it to us: 'Abthar informed us, from al-'Ala' ibn al-Musayyab; (H) and Harun ibn Sa'id al-Ayli narrated to me: Ibn Wahb narrated to us: Malik—who is Ibn Anas—narrated to me—all of them from Suhayl, with this chain of transmission, except that the hadith of al-'Ala' ibn al-Musayyab contains no mention of hatred.

Zuhayr ibn Harb narrated to us: Jarir narrated to us, from Suhayl, from his father, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "Indeed, when Allah loves a servant, He calls Gabriel and says: 'Indeed, I love so-and-so, so love him.' He said: So Gabriel loves him. Then he calls out in heaven, saying: 'Indeed, Allah loves so-and-so, so love him.' And the inhabitants of heaven love him. He said: Then acceptance is placed for him on earth. And when He hates a servant, He calls Gabriel and says: 'Indeed, I hate so-and-so, so hate him.' He said: So Gabriel hates him. Then he calls out among the inhabitants of heaven: 'Indeed, Allah hates so-and-so, so hate him.' He said: And they hate him, and then hatred is placed for him on earth."

Qutaybah ibn Sa'id and Zuhayr ibn Harb narrated to us, they said: Jarir narrated to us, from Talq ibn Mu'awiyah al-Nakha'i Abu Ghiyath, from Abu Zur'ah ibn 'Amr ibn Jarir, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: A woman came to the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) with a son of hers and said: "O Messenger of Allah, he is ailing, and I fear for him, and I have already buried three." He said: "You have indeed protected yourself with a mighty shield against the Fire." Zuhayr said: from Talq, and did not mention the kunya.

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah, Muhammad ibn 'Abdillah ibn Numayr, and Abu Sa'id al-Ashajj narrated to us—and the wording is Abu Bakr's—they said: Hafs narrated to us—meaning Ibn Ghiyath; (H) and 'Umar ibn Hafs ibn Ghiyath narrated to us: my father narrated to us, from his grandfather Talq ibn Mu'awiyah, from Abu Zur'ah ibn 'Amr ibn Jarir, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: A woman came to the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) with a young boy of hers and said: "O Prophet of Allah, supplicate to Allah for him, for indeed I have buried three." He said: "You have buried three?" She said: "Yes." He said: "You have indeed protected yourself with a mighty shield against the Fire." 'Umar alone among them said: from his grandfather, while the rest said: from Talq, and did not mention the grandfather.

Suwayd ibn Sa'id and Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us—and they were close in wording—they said: al-Mu'tamir narrated to us, from his father, from Abu al-Salil, from Abu Hassan, who said: I said to Abu Hurayrah: "Two sons of mine have died; will you not narrate to me a hadith from the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) by which you comfort our hearts concerning our deceased?" He said: He said: "Yes, their young ones are the little free-roaming children of Paradise; one of them meets his father—or he said: his parents—and takes hold of his garment—or he said: of his hand—just as I take hold of the hem of this garment of yours, and he does not let go—or he said: does not cease—until Allah admits him and his father into Paradise." And in the narration of Suwayd: he said: Abu al-Salil narrated to us. And 'Ubaydullah ibn Sa'id narrated it to me: Yahya—meaning Ibn Sa'id—narrated to us, from al-Taymi, with this chain of transmission, and he said: "Did you hear anything from the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) by which you comfort our hearts concerning our deceased?" He said: "Yes."

Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna and Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, they said: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us; (H) and 'Ubaydullah ibn Mu'adh narrated to us: my father narrated to us: Shu'bah narrated to us, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Asbahani, in this chain of transmission, with the like of its meaning; and they both added from Shu'bah, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Asbahani, who said: I heard Abu Hazim narrating from Abu Hurayrah that he said: "Three who have not reached the age of puberty (al-hinth)."

Abu Kamil al-Jahdari Fudayl ibn Husayn narrated to us: Abu 'Awanah narrated to us, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Asbahani, from Abu Salih Dhakwan, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, who said: A woman came to the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) and said: "O Messenger of Allah, the men have taken all your speech, so appoint for us a day from yourself when we may come to you and you teach us of what Allah has taught you." He said: "Gather on such-and-such day." So they gathered, and the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) came to them and taught them of what Allah had taught him. Then he said: "There is no woman among you who precedes with three of her children but they will be a shield for her from the Fire." A woman said: "And two? And two? And two?" The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "And two, and two, and two."

Qutaybah ibn Sa'id narrated to us: 'Abd al-'Aziz—meaning Ibn Muhammad—narrated to us, from Suhayl, from his father, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said to women of the Ansar: "No woman among you loses three children and seeks the reward of Allah for them, except that she will enter Paradise." A woman among them said: "Or two, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "Or two."

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah, 'Amr al-Naqid, and Zuhayr ibn Harb narrated to us, they said: Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah narrated to us; (H) and 'Abd ibn Humayd and Ibn Rafi' narrated to us from 'Abd al-Razzaq: Ma'mar informed us—both from al-Zuhri, with Malik's chain of transmission and with the meaning of his hadith, except that in the hadith of Sufyan: "so that he enters the Fire except for the expiation of the oath."

Yahya ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: I read to Malik, from Ibn Shihab, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), who said: "No one among the Muslims loses three children and the Fire touches him, except for the expiation of the oath."

'Amr al-Naqid narrated to me: Abu Ahmad al-Zubayri narrated to us: Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz narrated to us, from 'Ubaydullah ibn Abi Bakr ibn Anas, from Anas ibn Malik, who said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "Whoever raises two girls until they reach maturity, he and I will come on the Day of Resurrection like this"—and he joined his fingers together.
